title: Netanyahu Orders Large-Scale Military Operation in West Bank
gist: After two Israeli soldiers were killed near Hebron, Netanyahu ordered a sweeping West Bank operation then partly scaled it back to a cordon, days before Israel's election. The brief also covers Typhoon Champi, a Tibet quake and Brazil's tied runoff.

insights.claim: Netanyahu vowed the largest West Bank operation since 1967 after a checkpoint shooting near Hebron killed two soldiers, then softened to considering a cordon around Hebron and Halhul.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Escalation days before the Oct. 27 vote raises regional risk.
insights.quote: We will evacuate the residents, go house to house

insights.claim: The plan mirrors early-2025 Jenin operations, which demolished hundreds of homes and displaced thousands, and critics saw it as a political lifeline for Netanyahu.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Military action may serve coalition politics.

insights.claim: Netanyahu faces a vote seen as a referendum on Gaza, Lebanon and Iran wars and likely needs the hard right, including annexation backers, and pledged to expand settlements.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp

insights.claim: Typhoon Champi killed at least one person, injured about 160, plunged more than 77,000 Taiwan homes into darkness and led to nearly 1,000 flight cancellations.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Short-term disruption to Taiwan operations and logistics.

insights.claim: A UN report says Earth is on track for 2.6 degrees Celsius of warming by 2100 if all countries meet Paris pledges, which is considered unlikely.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Pledges fall well short of the 1.5C goal.

insights.claim: A 7.0 earthquake in Tibet killed at least 16, destroyed about 340 homes in Nagqu and displaced more than 12,000.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp

insights.claim: Brazil's runoff is tied at 50 percent of valid votes per Datafolha, with Flavio ahead by 1 point in total votes; first round was 47.03 percent versus 45.16 percent.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: A coin-flip race; a Bolsonaro win adds to Latin America's far-right wave.
